pr_title: Dockerfile: use TARGETPLATFORM to build Docker
pr_body:
follow-up #43529
~needs https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/44513~

fixes https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/41590
fixes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/41862
fixes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/41519
fixes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/39380
closes https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/43492
closes https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/43613

Better support for cross compilation so we can fully rely on `--platform` flag of buildx for a seamless integration.

This removes unnecessary extra cross logic in the Dockerfile, removes `DOCKER_CROSSPLATFORMS` and `CROSS` vars and some hack scripts as well.

Non-sandboxed build invocation is still supported and dev stages in the Dockerfile have been updated accordingly.

Bake definition and GitHub Actions workflows have been updated accordingly as well.

cc @thaJeztah @rumpl @vvoland
pr_comments:
> I didn't get past the first commit. There are so many behaviour changes to the `hack/make` scripts which have nothing to do with the PR description _or commit message_.

@corhere Yes this was indeed ahead of the expectations, sorry about that. It should be easier to review now.
Opened https://github.com/docker/docker-ce-packaging/pull/801 to check if packaging is still working with this PR.

Thanks! @corhere approved this PR earlier, and changes since his last review were removing some changes (related to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/44722).

I asked @rumpl to do another review, to have the extra eyes before I merge; let's get this one in 👍
oh! didn't expect you to  be online, @corhere 😂  thanks!

## Describe the results you expected:

The windows binaries to be built under `bundles/cross/windows/amd64/`
I can get this to work if I change this line https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/Makefile#L251 to set DOCKER_CROSSPLATFORMS before the docker command:
`DOCKER_CROSSPLATFORMS=windows/amd64; $(DOCKER_RUN_DOCKER) hack/make.sh cross`

review_comments:
ISTR we kept this field in `dockerversion` with the intent to (potentially) surface this information in `docker version` / `docker info` and/or `--version` output to help debugging issues when users report issues (it would save us to ask "is this a static binary, or did you install from deb/rpm?").

I don't think we ever did this, but perhaps still something to consider.
